cluster_name: Hamas agrees to disarm under Trump plan as Israel raises objections
tldr: Headlines split across two dominant registers that map cleanly onto geopolitics: outlets in China, Russia, Iran, and Qatar lead with kill counts and Israeli strikes as the week's primary fact, while Western, Turkish, and pan-Arab outlets foreground the Netanyahu-Trump political friction over deal terms. The sequencing impasse — disarmament preconditions withdrawal — surfaces as a distinct third register in Israeli, Qatari, pan-African, and Hong Kong headlines, making the structural deadlock visible at the homepage layer. Tehran Times is the only outlet whose headline assigns explicit motive to Israeli strikes ('to quash Hamas's disarmament plan'), a causal claim absent even in pan-Arab coverage. Egypt Independent is the only outlet making Netanyahu's silence the headline event itself, framing the absence of a statement as deliberate political action.
event_summary: Hamas agreed on July 31 to disarm and transfer weapons to a Palestinian governing committee under Trump's Board of Peace roadmap; Israel raised security concerns and continued airstrikes that killed dozens of Palestinians in the days following.

single_outlet_findings.finding: Only headline in the corpus to assign explicit motive to Israeli strikes — 'to quash Hamas's disarmament plan' — treating the strikes as deliberate sabotage of the deal rather than parallel operations; this causal framing is absent even in pan-Arab outlets.

Only headline making Netanyahu's three-day public silence the news event itself, framing the absence of a statement as a deliberate political act rather than a secondary detail; all other outlets headline the security concerns he eventually communicated.

'Truce talks remain deadlocked' is the most sceptical headline characterisation by any non-hostile outlet on Aug 3 — directly contradicting deal-progress claims issued by the Board of Peace that same week.

Only headline foregrounding the Gazan civilian perspective — 'Gazans say Trump's touting of plan jars with grim reality' — a lived-experience register absent from all 24 other headlines in the corpus.
Only headline casting doubt on the deal's viability via direct question — 'will Hamas actually disarm in Gaza?' — making scepticism about implementation surface-visible at the RSS/homepage layer.

bottom_line: At the headline layer, the corpus splits into two nearly equal halves: outlets in China, Russia, Iran, and Qatar lead with Israeli kill counts as the week's defining fact, while Western and pan-Arab outlets lead with Netanyahu-Trump political friction — with the sequencing deadlock (disarmament before withdrawal) most plainly stated in Israeli, Qatari, pan-African, and Hong Kong headlines.
